s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic, violaceous, annular skin lesions in a localized area
salient_findings: Discrete, dark red, circular lesions in the right axilla
Severe pruritus at the lesion sites
Lesions are well-circumscribed, violaceous, and annular without scale or erosion
key_facts: Male patient in his 40s
3-month history of skin lesions
Lesions are limited to the right axilla
Severe pruritus wakes the patient up at night
No recent trauma or history of similar lesions
No associated pain, blisters, or systemic symptoms
No improvement with over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream, ketoconazole cream, or discontinuation of underarm deodorant
Biopsy findings show lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction
Wood lamp examination was negative

shortlist.label: Granuloma annulare
shortlist.why_kept: Annular skin lesions with lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction on biopsy

shortlist.label: Lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic, violaceous, annular skin lesions in a localized area with negative Wood lamp examination

shortlist.label: Annular lichenoid dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to lichen planus with annular lesions and pruritus

shortlist.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
shortlist.why_kept: Annular skin lesions with centrifugal spread and pruritus

shortlist.label: Contact dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Localized skin lesions in the axilla with severe pruritus, potentially due to allergen or irritant exposure

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of discrete, dark red, circular lesions in the right axilla with severe pruritus and the biopsy findings of lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction are most consistent with annular lichenoid dermatitis, which is a condition characterized by annular or oval patches with a violaceous border and a tendency to occur in the axillary region.

rejected.label: Granuloma annulare
rejected.why: Typically presents with papular lesions in a ring-like pattern, often on the hands or feet, which does not match the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: Usually involves the mucous membranes and other areas of the body, and the lesions are often accompanied by scaling or erosion, which is not seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
rejected.why: Characterized by rapidly expanding, annular lesions with a trailing scale, which is not consistent with the patient's stable, well-circumscribed lesions.

rejected.label: Contact dermatitis
rejected.why: The patient's lack of response to discontinuation of underarm deodorant and the specific biopsy findings make this diagnosis less likely.
